This tutorial provides a step-by-step guide to creating a local Git repository and pushing it to your GitHub account. It covers initializing a project folder, linking it to a remote GitHub repository, and committing your files. You will also learn how to update your repository when changes are made locally. These commands are beginner-friendly and can be directly copied and executed in your terminal. By the end, you'll have your project successfully version-controlled and hosted on GitHub.

---

## Create a New Local Project

```bash
mkdir my_project                  # Create project folder
cd my_project                     # Navigate into folder
git init                          # Initialize Git
```

```bash
echo "# My Project" >> README.md  # Create a README file
```

```bash
git add README.md                 # Stage file
git commit -m "Initial commit"    # Commit file
```

---

## Link to GitHub Repository

(Create a repository on GitHub first: [https://github.com/new](https://github.com/new))

### Method 1: Using HTTPS
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/<username>/my_project.git
```

### Method 2: Using SSH (if keys are configured)
```bash
git remote add origin git@github.com:<username>/my_project.git
```

---

## Push Code to GitHub

```bash
git branch -M main                # Ensure branch is 'main'
git push -u origin main           # Push to GitHub
```

---

## Update Changes to GitHub Later

When you make changes locally:
```bash
git status                        # Check modified files
git add .                         # Stage all changes
git commit -m "Describe your changes here"
git push                          # Push updates to GitHub
```

---

## Clone an Existing Repository (Optional)

If you want to work on an existing repo:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/<username>/existing_repo.git
cd existing_repo
```

Make changes, then:
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Updated files"
git push
```
